newsitem.title: CHINA: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) mostly up.
newsitem.headline: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) mostly up.

text.p: Following is the China Interbank Offered Rate (CHIBOR) for Monday issued by the official Xinhua news agency on behalf of the People's Bank of China, the central bank.
The figures represent weighted averages and not closing prices and are annual percentage rates.
Turnover soared to 4.186 billion yuan from 725 million yuan last Friday with the 20-day contract the most actively traded.
The market was active on Monday with state banks and short-term financial centres -- money brokerages run by the central bank -- traded heavily, traders said.
The major factor behind the activity was the recently increased fund demand from grain producing provinces due to the approach of the summer harvest season, they said.
"The provinces usually need more money to puchase grain from the farmers on the summer harvest season," one trader said.
"They borrowed heavily on Monday, in particular through the short-term financial centres," he said.
Jiangxi and Hunan centers were the most active borrowers while the centres in Shanghai and Beijing were the major net lenders, traders said.
Traders said they believed the interbank rates would move up slightly up in active trading in the next few days.
